{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Desserts|Desserts]] | [[Cookbook:Confections|Confections]]

'''Chocolate truffles''' are soft chocolate balls. This recipe makes about 24.

==Ingredients==
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (227 [[Cookbook:g|g]]) bittersweet/plain [[Cookbook:Chocolate|chocolate]], chopped into small pieces
*6 imperial [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (7.2 US tablespoons / 108 ml) [[Cookbook:Double Cream|double cream]] (48% fat)
*[[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|Cocoa powder]]
*[[Cookbook:Icing sugar|Icing sugar]]

==Procedure==
# Put the chocolate in a bowl and set over (a [[Cookbook:Double Boiler|double boiler]]).
# Heat until melted and smooth, stirring occasionally.
# Remove from the pot of hot water.
# Add the cream and stir well. Leave to cool.
# Cover and refrigerate for 35 minutes or until the mixture is just firm enough to hold its shape.
# [[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] a layer of cocoa powder and icing sugar together onto a plate. The icing sugar is to make sure the cocoa powder isn't too bitter.
# Take a heaped [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoonful]] of the chocolate mixture and shape it into a ball.
# Roll each truffle in the cocoa powder/icing sugar to coat all over in an even layer. Shake off the excess and set on a tray.
# Continue shaping and coating the remaining truffles. Set on a tray, making sure they don't touch each other.
# Cover and refrigerate. Remove 15 minutes before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* '''Vanilla truffles:''' Use white chocolate, reducing the icing sugar to preference. Add about ½ tablespoon of [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]].
* '''Lime:''' Use white chocolate, reducing icing sugar content to preference. Add about ¾–1 of a tablespoon of diluted lime cordial, and a couple of pinches of ground lime zest.
* In the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|USA]], try using 2 tablespoons unsalted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] with 5 ⅓ tablespoons heavy cream to replace the double cream.
